articleTitle: Passive RFID Tag for Respiratory Frequency Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: Continuous monitoring of vital signals provides relevant information about a patient health status, which is essential in situations of risk. There is a need for practical and efficient systems to obtain these parameters and the RFID technology is presented here as a solution. In this work, a passive RFID tag is developed for respiratory rate monitoring. The RFID tag is a wireless solution for the subject and provides comfort due to its flexibility. Simulations and measurements were performed. To carry out the simulations, it was necessary to characterize the dielectric materials. The principle of operation of the technology in this application is based on the variations of the Received Signal Strength Indicator (RSSI) caused by the respiratory movements. As a result of the measurements performed with the tag placed on the abdomen of a person, during which forced inhalations and slow expirations were made, these variations of the RSSI could be noticed and, based on the respiratory cycles detected, it was possible to estimate the respiratory rate.

articleTitle: A New System for All-optical AND Logic gate on Semiconductor Optical Amplifier based Michelson
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: In this paper, the semiconductor optical amplifier (SOA) is used with a Michelson interferometer (MI) forming a structure of SOA-MI logic devices with symmetrically identical Fiber Bragg Grating (FBG) at the output of each of its arms, to a numerical simulation of the all-optical AND logic gate of two binary input data signals with different bit numbers using crossgain modulation (XGM) technique at 10 Gb/s bit rate and filter bandwidth at 10, 20 and 40 GHz using OptiSystem 15.0 software from OptiWave Corporation, to demonstrate and extract simple design rules for high-speed optical processing and analysis of non-linear SOA-induced properties. In addition, this work includes the study of the effect of bandwidth and number of bits on received power, minimum bit error rate (BER) and maximum quality factor (Q-factor) and Optical Signal to Noise Ratio (OSNR). We run the SOA-MI-based AND logic gate with some parameters and the results can demonstrate a structure of highperformance optical logic devices with high speed.

articleTitle: Big Data Analytics of Smart Grids using Artificial Intelligence for the Outliers Correction at Demand Measurements
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: Smart grids are increasingly present to improve the energy efficiency of the electrical network and several equipment are fundamental in this process, among them smart meters. Such devices accumulate an enormous flow of information that can be analyzed to aid in the decision making of the electric system controllers. This makes the concept of Big Data Analytics present, capable of processing various data and correcting atypical values, called outiliers, through algorithms using artificial intelligence, such as Fuzzy logic and Artificial Neural Networks. As a way of improving existing results, the present work suggests the use of a hybrid algorithm, the Adaptive Neuro Fuzzy Inference System (ANFIS). This algorithm showed better performance in the correction of outliers when compared with techniques based on Artificial Neural Networks and Linear Interpolation. Finally, results of the estimations will be presented using real energy demand data for a substation of electricity distribution.

articleTitle: Wavelet Total Variation Method Applied to Partial Discharge Signal Denoising
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: Signal processing techniques are used with the purpose of assisting in the process of equipment maintenance, avoiding failures and unwanted stops. One such fault is known as Partial Discharge (PD). The objective of this work is to evaluate the denoising performance of the Wavelet Total Variation method when applied to synthetic and laboratorial PD signals corrupted by Gaussian, harmonic and impulsive noises, as a way to improve their measurement conditions. The results obtained are promising and show that the method reconstructs the signal, maintaining just the discharges.

articleTitle: Optoacoustic intelligent sensor for real-time detection of fruit flies in McPhail traps
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: This work presents the development of an optoacoustic sensor for use in intelligent traps with real-time detection of fruit flies Ceratitis capitata and Anastrepha fraterculus to be used in a McPhail kind trap. The sensor uses an array of infrared LED light source and photodiodes to make a light courtain. Fluctuation caused by the beating of insect wings and are detected by the sensor. The flying pattern of the flies ensures the flies will pass through sensor once. The captured signal is conditioned by the sensor hardware and is used to characterize the insect species for future classification and counting. The sensor is designed to be used in McPhail type traps and it is not a trap by itself. The sensor performance was evaluated through simulated experiments in the laboratory, where it proved to be promising for use with the insects of interest.

articleTitle: Low-cost circular-polarizared patch antenna for RFID applications
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: In this paper, a low-cost patch antenna with circular polarization using a FR4 substrate is proposed. The antenna was developed to be used in US standard UHF RFID application, with better impedance matching at 915MHz. The design was concepted and optimized through simulations using the ANSYS HFSS software. The simulation results presented an absolute gain of 5.76dB, an axial ratio of 1.87dB and the return loss (S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>) of 48dB at 915MHz. The antenna was manufactured and measurements of the return loss using the Keysight Vector Network Analyzer were made to compare with the simulation results. Furthermore, it was compared to a commercial antenna by reading a commercial tag using a RFID reader in order to validate the proposed antenna application.

articleTitle: A new low power and all-MOS voltage-to-current converter for current mode ADCs with high linearity, high bandwidth and rail-to-rail input range
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: This work presents a new low power and all-MOS voltage-to-current (V-I) converter with high linearity (≃0.15%), high bandwidth (≃19 MHz) and rail-to-rail input range (from V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">SS</sub> up to V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">DD</sub>) to be used prioritarily as a internal building block of current mode A/D converters. The text includes the description of the constituent stages of the converter topology, as well as the static and dynamic simulations results, validating the proposed converter through the MOS-level implementation using computing tool Pyxis Schematics from Mentor Graphics, with XFAB 180 nm technology.

articleTitle: Using Metamaterial Complementary Split-Ring Resonators for Measuring Dielectric Constants and Loss Tangents at 22 GHz
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: This paper presents a method using a metamaterial complementary split-ring resonator (CSRR) to measure the dielectric constant (Dk) and loss tangent (Df) of materials at a frequency of 22 GHz. The method involves calculating the permittivity of an unknown material based on the oscillation frequency changes of a CSRR, which is caused by the material under test. This method with a CSSR sensor uses only the resonance frequency and the S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</sub> magnitude response at the resonance frequency to calculate Dk and Df. The measurement accuracy was assessed by comparing the results with the declared values specified in the datasheets of material manufacturers. The results show good agreement with the declared values in the datasheets. Thus, with this method, the dielectric properties of materials at high frequencies of millimeter waves (mm-waves) can be characterized and a non-destructive sensor can be built.

articleTitle: High-Q MEMS Ring Resonator Design for Multi-band Filter Application
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: This paper presents a methodology for the design of a multi-band MEMS resonator with quality factor in the order of tens of thousands to serve as a filter in communication applications. The design was based in a three concentric ring resonator already fabricated by the group. The methodology allows designing devices for any resonating frequencies within those bounded by construction constraints of the fabrication process. The methodology is further corroborated by the design and simulation of a device with resonating frequencies at 90 kHz, 135 kHz and 180 kHz and quality factor not lower than 18,000.

articleTitle: Modeling a Multi-Echo Ultrasonic Waves Propagation using 2D Ray-Tracing Method
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: Ultrasonic transducers have been used for applications in several areas of engineering. Specifically, in the wind energy sector, ultrasonic transducers are used to measure wind speed. The principle of measurement is based on the estimation of time of flight (ToF). The estimation of this magnitude may be influenced by medium noises, but new approaches to analysis and advanced measurement techniques are considering the influence of multiechoes on the measurement environment. In this sense, this article aims to develop a computational tool for modeling the propagation of ultrasonic waves in closed environments using the Ray-Tracing technique. Results of the wind speed measurement method will be presented using 2 axes considering different noise levels of the medium, as well as a different number of reflections. The ToF estimation technique used was the Threshold, and the signal analysis was performed in the time and frequency domain.

articleTitle: Analytical Modeling for the Characterization of On-Chip Spiral Inductor in 0.13 μm
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: In this paper, we present the modeling for a rapid characterization of integrated spiral inductors. Closed-form has been used to estimate the parameters of the equivalent circuit, which are calculated as a function of the parameters of the inductor physical design. The double-π equivalent circuit was adopted to model the physical phenomena resulting from electromagnetic coupling and high-frequency operation. The method for calculating the oxide capacitance has included the contribution of the fringing electric fields for better prediction of the inductor characteristics. In order to verify the performed modeling, a set of octagonal on-chip spiral inductors with different geometries were simulated in the Momentum ADS and the main figures of merit of the inductor were compared. The mean error between the model and EM simulation was 3.6% for the DC inductance, 7.7% for the maximum value of the quality factor and 1.3% for the self-resonance frequency.

articleTitle: Exploring Autonomic Sensors Processing in the Internet of Things
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: Advances in the Internet of Things (IoT) allowed different sources of distributed contextual information, through sensors, to become available to the applications, enabling the creation of more sophisticated models to identify situations of interest. The use of middlewares is highlighted in the literature as a way to handle the distribution of devices in IoT and also to make sensors processing more transparent to applications. Considering this scenario, the objective of this work is the design of an architecture focused on the management and composition of sensors processing flows. This architecture provides situation awareness and autonomous management of context source devices (sensors) to an application in the healthcare area targeted to patients in cardiac rehabilitation.

articleTitle: Parameterized FPGA Implementation of a Real-time Discrete Wavelet Transform Processor
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: This paper proposes and evaluates a parameterized Field Programmable Fate Array (FPGA) implementation of a Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT) processor for streaming digital signal processing applications. Parameterization occurs during synthesis time and with respect to the number of decomposition levels and wavelet filters. Both parameters are taken into account to synthesize the group delay compensation module. The implementation of several wavelet families with varied number of decomposition levels and filter sizes was evaluated according to FPGA resource utilization and operating frequency. It was observed that the proposed architecture is resource constrained by the number of DSP blocks in the FPGA and time constrained by the routing delay of larger implementations. The system was tested operating at full analog-to-digital converter data rate (245.76 MHz) in a signal de-noising application.

articleTitle: Gain and offset calibration for an Analog-to-Information Converter
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: Analog-to-information converters (AIC) are physical implementations of Compressed Sensing that have been proposed to overcome the technological limitations of the analog-to-digital converters (ADC) in terms of bandwidth and quantity of data produced after conversion. The AIC hardware suffers from non-idealities of components and subsystems, which reduces the quality of the measured signal reconstruction. Such effects can be compensated by calibration that normally have been implemented in the signal recovery methods. In this paper, we analyze a calibration method for AIC that takes into account only the measurements produced by the AIC. Results show that the hardware calibration improves the signal reconstruction with regard to signal-to-noise and distortion ratio (SINAD), independent of the reconstruction algorithm.

articleTitle: Study of the Discretization Process applied to Continuous Random Variables in the Density Estimation Context
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: The following topics are dealt with: analogue-digital conversion; low-power electronics; CMOS digital integrated circuits; radiofrequency identification; current-mode circuits; integrated circuit design; photomultipliers; nuclear electronics; readout electronics; power consumption.

articleTitle: Ionization Current Detection for Homogeneous Charge Compression Ignition (HCCI) on Dual Mode Engines Using a Compact Flyback Circuit
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: This work discusses the detection of ionization current for Homogeneous Charge Compression Ignition (HCCI) on dual mode engines using a compact and versatile flyback circuit. Since spark plugs come already incorporated in the engines, they are commonly used for sensing the ionization current to monitor Spark Ionization (SI) and HCCI systems. The main challenge of this work was to propose a compact and versatile flyback circuit coupled to an ion measuring stage to monitor the ionization current to control HCCI systems. For the experimental validation of the proposed flyback circuit, the spark plug was implemented with the aid of a metallic needle positioned at different distances from a ground plane by means of a micrometer screw in order to vary the ionization current in the range of 1μA to 2mA. As a result, besides being compact, the proposed flyback circuit was improved with a low pass RC filter at its output, which meant a peak-to-peak output voltage ripple below 1.5% in relation to the maximum DC output voltage controlled in the range of 200 to 700V.

articleTitle: Instrumentation and Algorithms for the Sonification of Scanning Probe Microscopy Output
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: The present work reports on the development of scientific instrumentation in scanning probe microscopy (SPM), a field of wide application and versatility that allows exploring surface properties at the atomic and molecular levels. Usually, SPM systems deliver information to the user with images that represent the surface properties. Here we implemented a realtime data sonification system that enables visually impaired people to perform SPM experiments and provides other information that is not nicely captured by the human eye. Based on a Raspberry Pi 3B + board and Python algorithms, our system generates parameters based on an SPM scan for sonification that is tested here using the MIDI (Musical Instrument Digital Interface).

articleTitle: Test Method for AIC based on extension IEEE Std. 1241 Sine-wave Fit using Multi-Sine Signals
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: Analog-to-information converters (AIC) are devices that implement the compressive sensing theory, and are applied on sparse signals. There are some AIC architectures and several implementations have been already developed. However, few methods to test these devices have been proposed. In this paper, an adaptation of the extension IEEE Std. 1241 Sine-wave Fit using multi-sine signals is proposed for AIC testing. The main aim of the proposed test is to extract the Signal-to-Noise and Distortion Ratio (SINAD) from an implemented AIC directly from its measurements using multi-sine signals without requiring signal reconstruction. The implemented AIC was a configurable one based on the Random Modulation Pre-Integrator (RMPI) architecture. The obtained results validate the proposed test by comparing them to the SINAD and the Mean Square Error (MSE) values of the reconstructed signal, and also confirms that the performance of the AIC is directly proportional to the sparsity of the input signal, since the SINAD drops with the increase of the number of spectral components of the input signals, i.e with the decrease of sparsity.

articleTitle: Modelling and Estimation of the Oxygen Transfer Function in a Bioreactor with Aeration Driven by PWM Signal
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: The dissolved oxygen concentration is a critical variable to the aerobic biological processes and, hence, the rate of oxygen transfer from gas phase to the liquid phase, where the biological reactions are taking place, is an important issue. The gas-liquid oxygen transfer process is characterized by the volumetric mass transfer coefficient, or oxygen transfer function, which is a parameter that has been used in the design, operation and optimization of such processes. For practical purposes, the oxygen transfer function is considered to depend only on the aerators inlet airflow rate, which is typically nonlinear. In this paper, a linear model of the oxygen transfer function is proposed, where the aerators are driven in a PWM mode rather than in a variable flow rate. Results from experiments with clean water and activated sludge samples show the validity of the proposed linear model.

articleTitle: A Less Complex and Effective Approach to Design Current Sample-and-Hold Circuits with Clock Generation for use on Current Mode ADCs
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: This work presents a less complex and effective approach to design current sample-and-hold (S&H) circuits with reduced switching noise, charge injection and clock feed-through effects, based on the combination of three known simple techniques. The circuit proposed was designed to be used prioritarily as an internal building block of current mode A/D converters. This project also covers the development of all needed circuits for clock signals generation. The text includes the description of the constituent stages of the current sample and hold circuit topology, as well as the static and dynamic simulations results, validating the proposed converter through the MOS-level implementation using computing tool Pyxis Schematics from Mentor Graphics, with XFAB 180 nm technology.

articleTitle: ν-Angra Readout Electronics and Target Detector Assessment using a Cosmic Rays based Trigger
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: In this work, a battery of measurements have been carried out with the objective of characterizing the target detector of the Neutrinos Angra Experiment using a cosmic rays based trigger. It is its first assessment after the detector was fully equipped with all the 32 PMTs, as foreseen by the project, and its custom-based readout electronics. The ν-Angra detector was constructed with the purpose of measuring antineutrinos particles generated in the fission process of the Angra dos Reis Nuclear Reactor. Before transporting it to the nuclear reactor facility, it is important to measure its operational characteristics as a first step of the commissioning stage. The achieved results describing some of the main characteristics of the detector system are presented in this document.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Density and Temperature Invariant Displacer-Type Liquid Level Measuring Method
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: A new displacer-type liquid level measuring method has been proposed by Souza, Carvalho and Canuto [1], this method was tested through computer simulation and results indicate that it has a high linearity besides being ideally insensitive to fluid temperature and density. However, these simulations disregarded some characteristics of the method implementation. In this paper we analyze the influence of buoyancy on the rod that connects the displacer to the load cell (see Fig. 2), and of the presence of a second phase in the liquid tank. Finally, we present and test a sensor prototype. Simulation results show that the rod buoyancy introduces a non-linearity in the system and the second phase adds a small measurement error. Real experiments indicate that the sensor prototype can be used in order to test the effectiveness of the method proposed in [1].

articleTitle: Large AC testing of PN junction diodes
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: Circuit project demands high quality device parameters data. The measurements of these parameters often require precise measurements instrumentation as well as the use of advanced data analysis. One of the simplest and most common devices - the junction diode - remarkable has no published large signal AC data experimental analysis able to retrieve its physical parameters. In this work we present a sequence of measurements performed on typical diode, the 1N4007, subjected to a large AC signal and compare its response to a theoretical model for the time-dependent diode voltage equation. In addition, a Fourier analysis of the measured data was also performed. As a result, we were able to get dc parameters and its effective capacitance.

articleTitle: A Fully Passive UHF RFID Soil Moisture Time-Domain Transmissometry Based Sensor
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: In this work, it is proposed the integration of a time-domain transmissometry soil moisture sensor with a fully passive UHF RFID tag. A coplanar waveguide based sensor is modeled and simulated, whereas the propagation signal delay was analyzed when the sensor is surrounded by several permittivity scenarios. It is also proposed a low power interface circuit that enables a UHF RFID tag to obtain data from the developed sensor, which is accessible by any standard reader. The proof of concept prototype was developed and tested on soil with different moisture and salinities. From the experiments, it was found that the proposed sensor presents similar behavior for the tests performed with distilled and saltwater solutions with conductivities up to 1584 μS/cm.

articleTitle: Finite Element Modelling design and optimization of Love Wave mesoporous transducers for biochemical detection in liquid medium
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: We study numerically by a Finite Element Modeling (FEM) approach the design and the optimization of a Love wave transducer coated with a mesoporous sensitive layer. This association could allow to realize an easy functionalizable transducer for biochemical detection in liquid medium. The FEM approach is a good way to design the transducer by estimating many physical parameters in order to obtain a device which could work properly for a given application. Especially, by using a porous layer coated on an acoustic Love wave transducer, we need to be sure that the propagation parameters are still compatible with a usable device. In this paper, after a description of the reduced finite element model of the Love wave transducer, we show that the first experimental results are in a good agreement with the simulations. An “ultra-reduced” FEM approach of the Love wave transducer is carried out for easier consideration of the porous sensitive coating. Finally, experimental transducers are coated with TiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> porous sensitive layers by the sol gel technique: the porosity is varied in the range from 10% to 25 %, the pore size from 10 nm to 200 nm, and the thickness from 100 nm to 500 nm. Simulated and experimental results are in good accordance, and allow us to conclude that such transducer could achieve a good propagation of the acoustic wave for biochemical sensing.

articleTitle: Cell Library Design for Ultra-Low Power Internet-of-Things Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: A wide range of applications in the field of the Internet-of-Things (IoT) possess only strongly limited energy resources. This rises the need for Ultra-Low Power (ULP) designs that enable processing with lowest energy consumption. This, however, comes at considerable performance costs. Consequently, there is a need for flexible design flows that enable the designer to select the best tradeoff between energy consumption and performance for the destined application. Towards this end, we present in this paper a complete flow for the design of a ULP standard cell library based on the subthreshold methodology. The flow considers both the selection of the appropriate technology parameters, like supply voltage and base sizing, as well as the actual design and characterization of the standard cells. Simulation results for an ARM-based processor and ITC'99 and EPFL benchmark circuits realized in a commercial 130 nm technology indicate a possible reduction of power consumption of several factors, while performance degrades between two and three orders of magnitude.

articleTitle: A new modular framework for implementing A/D converters in CMOS technology in current mode
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: This work presents a new modular method of Analog-to-digital conversion to be implemented in current-mode with CMOS technology. It is based on a conversion basic cell called “Bitcell”. The text includes the description of the conversion principle, the prior analysis of the errors inherent to the proposed technique, advantages and disadvantages of the method, as well as the modeling and simulation of the proposed method. The principle was validated through the MOS-level implementation of the all MOS Bitcell topology using two computing tools: Dolphin Integrations SMASH, using MOS devices models of the 130 nm Global Foundries technology; and Pyxis, from Mentor Graphics, using PDK XFAB 180 nm. Concluding the text, the results of the static and dynamic simulations of the Bitcell implementation are presented.

articleTitle: Signal simulation based on the characteristics of the ν-Angra Experiment’s readout electronics
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: The Neutrinos Angra (ν-Angra) Experiment has the objective of developing a compact surface detector capable of monitoring the activity of nuclear reactors. The collaboration ν-Angra makes use of the Geant4 package to simulate the interactions occurring inside the detector. The outcome of this Geant4-based software provides time, position and energy of photons that reach the detector sensors; therefore none information about the electrical signal formation is given. In this context, this work proposes a method to simulate the ν-Angra electrical signal coming out from the signal acquisition chain. such chain is composed of a photomultiplier, an amplifier-shaper circuit and an analog-to-digital converter. The characteristics of the proposed method will be described and its performance will be evaluated based on a comparison between its output response and the real signal, experimentally acquired.
